description: Outage-response experiment on the e003 two-site simulated cluster. Each seed is a 15-hour simulated window with its own synthetic job mix, synthetic weather and a randomly drawn schedule of cooling failures, breaker events, grid curtailments and hardware faults (some with precursors). Every number here is a simulation assumption, not a measurement.
assumptions: Everything in this file is a simulation setting. No number here is a measurement of a real cluster.

The two-site cluster, job generator, thermal, breaker and power parameters come from sim-scenario-v2.json (not edited here). Power levels are read through the simulator at run time, so a recalibration of the simulator scenario flows through.

Job durations are drawn log-uniform between 1800 s and 21600 s (the base scenario uses 3600 s to 172800 s) so that a 15-hour window holds dozens of jobs; the job mix is otherwise the base scenario's, including its 10 percent of two-shard jobs that already follow the averaging rule.
The simulated clock starts at 17:00 UTC (late morning to midday local time); heat-wave centers and amplitudes are chosen to fall inside the 15-hour window and are simulation assumptions.

Event rates, precursor probability, precursor lead times and strengths, durations and severities are simulation assumptions chosen to produce several events per window; they are not rates of real facilities.
Controller decisions, forecasts and warnings use a 600 s interval; the simulator control step is 60 s and the base step is 60 s (the sim-scenario-v2.json steps are 10 s and 1 s).
Warning horizon 6 steps x 600 s = 60 min; forecast context 18 steps x 600 s = 3 h, equal to the 3 h warm-up before the first scheduled event.

Probability levels for the supply-temperature and GPU-temperature anomaly channels are the largest value (calibration_quantile 1.0) seen in event-free runs on training seeds. Level of the GPU temperature channel is the throttle threshold of the simulator scenario; level of the breaker load channel is 1.0 (rack power above rating); level of the site channel is the grid import limit including announced curtailments.
recheckpoint_s, clear_decisions, max_pause_s and oracle_extra_lead_steps are response-policy design choices that are not tuned.
